extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and peer reviewers (especially in computer science) who read and review research papers
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, stepwise method (three-pass) for reading research papers to form high-level impressions, understand content, and deeply verify/replicate results — intended to guide readers and serve as an implicit reviewer rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Pass (~5–10 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: high-level picture. Read title, abstract, introduction. Read section and subsection headings. Read conclusion. Glance at references; mark ones you've already read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After this you should be able to answer the 5 Cs: Category, Context, Correctness, Contributions, Clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category (one of the 5 Cs)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 5 Cs to answer after the first pass: 'Category'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine what type of paper it is (as a high-level classification) so you know what to expect from its goals and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context (one of the 5 Cs)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 5 Cs to answer after the first pass: 'Context'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the paper relative to prior work and the problem area; identify what problem it addresses and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness (one of the 5 Cs)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 5 Cs to answer after the first pass: 'Correctness'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a high level, assess whether the claims appear plausible and whether there are obvious flaws; deeper verification happens in later passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions (one of the 5 Cs)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 5 Cs to answer after the first pass: 'Contributions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the main contributions claimed by the paper and whether they are clearly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (one of the 5 Cs)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 5 Cs to answer after the first pass: 'Clarity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the paper is well written and whether the organization helps the reader understand the contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Pass (~1 hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: grasp content but skip details. Examine figures, diagrams, illustrations carefully. Mark unread relevant references for later. Take notes, summarize main thrust with supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully inspect visuals (are axes labeled? error bars? statistically significant?), note which references to read next, and produce a summary of the paper's main argument and evidence. If you cannot grasp the paper after the second pass, set it aside for later, ask the authors, or acquire more background before continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Pass (~4–5 hours for a beginner, ~1 for an expert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: re-implement the paper. Identify and challenge every assumption. Note every reference for further reading. Think about how you would present the same idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through the paper in full detail so you could reconstruct its structure from memory, reproduce results or re-implement methods, and identify strong and weak points, missing citations, and unstated assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer effort expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for reviewers: plan for at least a Pass 2 effort when reviewing papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Pass 1 review is effectively a desk-rejection or accept-without-reading and is likely to produce low-quality reviews. Reviewers should invest the time to reach the level of understanding provided by the second pass (and the third pass for thorough evaluation).
